# Governance guard registry

<!-- Generated by coord/engine/scripts/guard-registry.js write from coord/engine/governance-guards.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

One machine-readable inventory of every governance guard and gate check that can refuse a governed verb or fail a gate. Documentation and measurement only: no guard's behaviour changes. Tiers are proposals (direction only, ADR 0021): reduced gates switch on only after this registry is reviewed and tier classification and affected-test selection are validated against full runs.

- Ticket: COORD-914. Decision: ADR 0021 (coord/docs/decisions/0021-governance-ceremony-is-tiered-by-risk-and-integration-is-a-separate-authority.md). Review date: 2027-02-06.
- Guards: 99 (T0: 61, T1: 26, T2: 12). Run `node coord/engine/scripts/guard-registry.js sites` for the scanned refusal sites.
- Measured gate costs come only from: remote gate of 2026-11-05 on tree 61bf80c0 (COORD-871..888 stack; n22 and n24 full suites with coverage and dual-release run in parallel on one host).

## Tiers

T0, T1 and T2 are PROPOSED review classifications, not enforcement thresholds. Under ADR 0021 no enforcement changes until this registry is reviewed and tier classification and affected-test selection are validated against full runs; until then every guard runs for every ticket. The proposal: a tier is the lowest ticket tier at which the guard would run (T0 every ticket, T1 for T1 and T2 tickets, T2 only for policy, trust, identity, upgrade, release and ADR tickets). Ownership, provenance and integration-safety guards stay enforced at every tier: they are marked always_enforced and classified T0.

## Changing this registry

Classification changes (tier, always_enforced, editions, proposed merges, retirement) need human-admin review through a governed ticket that cites ADR 0021. Adding a guard means adding its entry, with a guard:<id> marker or an anchor, in the same change. An intentional rewording of a refusal message must update that site's registry anchor in the same change: the completeness check failing on a stale anchor is the intended signal, not something to silence. Coverage baselines are never refreshed to accommodate markers; a marker that makes the ratchet report new uncovered code is moved or registered by anchor instead.

## What the completeness check covers

- refusal-call: a fail()/die()/refuse()/throw new X() call in coord/engine/scripts/** production code whose call text (up to 6 lines) says refuse/refused/refusing/refusal or "Review-plan blockers"
- refusal-text: a string literal with that wording outside a refusal call (message builders such as formatTreeMutationSafetyHazard)
- blocker-code: a `code: "<name>"` blocker pushed by the start, submit and review-plan readiness collectors (coord/engine/scripts/gates/**, review-plan-readiness.js, decomposition-proof-gate.js, gate-plan.js, governance-validation.js)
- deny-decision: a `decision: "deny"` result from a runtime-authority, auto-mode or containment policy
- wrapper: a shared guard helper defined as assert<Name>, collect<Name>Issues/Blockers or format/build<Name>Refusal (assertRegisteredBoundOwner, assertProductionLocForCloseout, the review-plan blocker collectors, seal and drift assertions)
- shell-fail: a `fail "..."` call in release/verify-dual-release.sh
- stage: dynamically dispatched gate stages — release/check-public-release.sh CHECKS, the test-runner overallPass terms, arch-checks CHECKS and verify-upgrade-bridge.sh steps
- Excluded paths: *.test.js, __fixtures__/, vendor/, node_modules/, coord/engine/scripts/guard-registry.js (the scanner), coord/engine/scripts/lifecycle-help.js (usage text only).
- @enterprise/<file> names a file in the Enterprise-only subtree; in a Community cut those entries are not checked (see Not covered).

## Not covered by the completeness check

- **Refusals without refusal wording outside a guard wrapper:** A fail()/throw whose message neither says refuse/refused nor sits in an assert*/collect*Issues wrapper is invisible to the wording scan (for example argument validation such as "<verb> requires <ticket-id>", and the co-located-writer message). The registry lists the known ones with marker:true locations, so their markers are enforced in that direction only; a new unworded refusal is not detected.
- **Enterprise-only guards in a Community cut:** The Community cut strips the Enterprise-only subtree, so its check does not see these entries; the donor and the Enterprise cut check them. Files there are named with the @enterprise/ prefix because the Community open-core scan forbids the subtree's path in shipped files. Entries: enterprise-policy-broker, enterprise-warehouse-identity.
- **Enterprise verifier result codes:** The Enterprise adapter authorization policy and the conformance-bundle and rehash verifiers return result codes rather than refusing a verb; they are scanned but contain no refusal-worded site today.
- **Verifier result codes:** Signature, attestation and conformance verifiers (journal-signing.js, conformance-attestation.js) return result codes rather than refusing a verb; their callers' refusals are scanned.
- **Verb dispatch tables:** cli.js and governance-mcp.js route verbs to handlers; the scan covers the guard sites those handlers reach, not the routing tables themselves.
- **coord/scripts shims and coord/scripts/hooks wrappers:** Shims are thin re-exports of engine modules (coord/engine/shim-registry.json); the engine targets are scanned.
- **Product repo gates:** Commands recorded with gov add-repo-gate are adopter-defined; only the repo-gate record guard is in scope.
- **Release scripts other than the listed stages:** release/build-public-release.sh, publish-*.sh, scan-*.sh and the release/*.js checkers are reached through check-public-release.sh stages; their internal fail paths are not scanned individually.
- **The out-of-tree remote gate kit:** The 2026-11-05 legacy-entrypoint script lived in a scratch kit, not the repository; the in-repo equivalent is verify-upgrade-bridge.sh step 6.
- **CI workflows:** .github workflows are not scanned.
- **Test-file assertions:** *.test.js files are excluded; they prove guards, they are not guards.

## Guards

### prompt-record — Prompt record at start (content, coverage, preconditions)

- **Tier (proposed):** T1. **Kind:** verb-guard. **Editions:** Community, Enterprise. **Verbs or stage:** start
- **Protective intent:** A ticket starts only from a registered prompt record: its content is usable (not a stub or placeholder), it has prompt coverage or an explicit waiver, and the preconditions it declares resolve on the integration branch, so agents do not act on empty, missing or stale instructions.
- **Answers:** COORD-813, COORD-023
- **Overlaps:** prompt-registration-integrity
- **Implementation:** `coord/engine/scripts/prompt-coverage.js` assertPromptRecord, verifyDeclaredPreconditions, collectPromptRecordBlockers, formatPromptContentRefusal
- **Cost:** 1 check per landing; time: unknown (unknown). Not measured.
- **Failure remedy:** coord/scripts/gov register-prompt <ticket> --body-file <file>, or the waiver command the refusal prints; for an unresolved precondition, fix the prompt's ## Preconditions section and re-register it with gov register-prompt
- **Retirement criteria:** Retire when prompt registration itself validates content and preconditions at write time and start can trust the stored record.
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

### prompt-registration-integrity — Prompt registration target safety

- **Tier (proposed):** T0. **Kind:** verb-guard. **Editions:** Community, Enterprise. **Verbs or stage:** register-prompt
- **Protective intent:** register-prompt never writes a closed ticket's prompt, a hard-linked target or a prompt shared by other tickets.
- **Answers:** No incident or ticket id is cited in the code; to be recorded at review.
- **Overlaps:** none recorded
- **Implementation:** `coord/engine/scripts/prompt-coverage.js` (anonymous)
- **Cost:** 1 check per landing; time: unknown (unknown). Not measured.
- **Failure remedy:** Use a distinct prompt path, or reopen the ticket through its governed verb first
- **Retirement criteria:** Keep: cheap file-safety check.
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

### adr-requirement — ADR requirement

- **Tier (proposed):** T2. **Kind:** verb-guard. **Editions:** Community, Enterprise. **Verbs or stage:** move-review, finalize
- **Protective intent:** A ticket that changes a decision surface records an ADR before review.
- **Answers:** No incident or ticket id is cited in the code; to be recorded at review.
- **Overlaps:** adr-compliance-closure, business-context-status, context-pack-ack
- **Implementation:** `coord/engine/scripts/gates/adr.js` collectAdrRequirementIssues
- **Cost:** 1 check per landing; time: unknown (unknown). Not measured.
- **Failure remedy:** coord/scripts/gov adr --title <title> --ticket <ticket>, then gov update-plan <ticket>
- **Retirement criteria:** Merge into one decision-context record (COORD-932 packet in coord/engine/scripts/decision-context.js; proposal still needs human review). (see review section).
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

### review-cycles — Self-review cycles

### sync-derived-recovery-proof — Sync adopts only exact derived regeneration from unchanged canonical inputs

- **Tier (proposed):** T0 (always enforced). **Kind:** verb-guard. **Editions:** Community, Enterprise. **Verbs or stage:** sync
- **Protective intent:** Under the journal lock, gov sync may adopt drift only when every snapshot difference is a supported generated projection whose bytes equal a read-only regeneration from unchanged canonical inputs (board, plan records, prompts, decisions, policy inputs); symlinks, executable generated files, missing or corrupt baselines and mixed edits refuse, and the proof is journaled once with old and new digests (COORD-935). A journal baseline that predates the rendering policy inputs (GOVERNANCE.md, project.config.js, board schemas) cannot prove recovery and still needs the reviewed packet-bound gov reconcile procedure; existing downstream wedges on such baselines are not unblocked automatically.
- **Answers:** COORD-935
- **Overlaps:** seal-journal-drift, sync-unapproved-drift, board-cli-journal-bypass
- **Implementation:** `coord/engine/scripts/journal.js` withGovernanceMutation (sync derived-recovery refusal); `coord/engine/scripts/derived-sync-recovery.js` proveDerivedSync
- **Cost:** 1 proof per gov sync over drift; time: unknown (unknown). Not measured; runs only when sync meets drift.
- **Failure remedy:** Restore accidental edits; inspect with coord/scripts/gov doctor and gov reconcile --scope derived --dry-run; semantic drift or a legacy/incomplete baseline needs gov reconcile --reason ... --human-admin-override ... --expect-paths-file <packet>
- **Retirement criteria:** Keep while generated views can feed back into canonical records.
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

COORD-1027 routes proposals through a closed target and schema validator, binds them to exact source bytes, and refuses unsupported computed testPolicy values; approval remains fail-closed without the trusted human-approval verifier. - **Retirement criteria:** Keep while the test policy accepts adopter overrides and human exceptions.
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

- **Retirement criteria:** Retire only when ALL hold, recorded in the ticket closeout (COORD-961): (1) v0.1.16 is out of support, evidenced by the 0.2.0 release (COORD-912) having shipped with a real adopter upgrade canary, so no supported adopter remains on v0.1.16; (2) the v0.1.16 bridge rollback regression is kept in-suite (coord/engine/scripts/coord-upgrade.test.js: the COORD-885 new-directory fixture and the COORD-961 rollback test, with the COORD-886 post-apply read test) so must_still_cover stays covered after removal. Until then the guard stays. As of 2026-11-14 neither holds: COORD-912 is todo and the package is still 0.1.16.
- **Review date:** 2027-02-06

## Review: proposed merges

### decision-context-record

- **Merge:** adr-requirement, adr-compliance-closure, business-context-status, context-pack-ack into one decision-context record per ticket, validated once at move-review; implemented as the versioned packet in coord/engine/scripts/decision-context.js (COORD-932, expands into adr_refs, decision_required, the business-context invariant and context_pack_ack; proposal still needs human review).
- **Rationale:** Four guards ask the same question (which decisions and context bind this change) through four plan fields and four blocker codes; the COORD-871..888 stack hit each separately.
- **Must still cover:** a decision-surface change without an ADR (gates/adr.js adr_required); review and closeout citing the binding ADR (COORD-430); business-context risk without a current pack (COORD-569); mandatory context-pack sections never acknowledged (COORD-557, COORD-572, COORD-612, COORD-723)

### integration-authority

- **Merge:** tree-mutation-safety, canonical-authority-write, co-located-writer into the integration-authority permission (COORD-915).
- **Rationale:** All three approximate who may write canonical state; none caught the 2026-11-05 remote sync --commit.
- **Must still cover:** sync --commit over another session's in-flight work (COORD-911, 2026-11-05 incident); canonical mutation from an ephemeral worktree; two sessions in one worktree (COORD-223)
